title: NOAA ERSSTv6 has a +0.064 C warm step in January 2017, partly reversed in September 2020 (60S-60N); six reference SST records and moored buoys show it, and it makes 2019 its false record year
abstract: Question: ERSSTv6 (August 2025) is now NOAA's official SST record and the base of NOAAGlobalTemp v6.1 and RONI. Does it have product-specific steps in 1982-2025? Approach: we added ERSSTv6 to a blind joint homogenisation of seven products (DOISST v2.1, ESA CCI v3, ERA5, COBE-SST2, ERSSTv5, HadISST1, OI SST v2) on one 60S-60N mask, with the unchanged method of sci:sha256:d9bdf1f8. We tested the steps against HadSST4.2, Argo and 131 moored buoys, which the search did not use, and computed the consequences. Results: ERSSTv6 has a warm step of +0.064 +/- 0.005 C (60S-60N; +0.081 C at 20S-20N) in January 2017 and a step of -0.029 +/- 0.005 C in September 2020. ERSSTv5 has neither. Against six references, ERSSTv6 minus reference rose by +0.042 to +0.074 C from 2013-2016 to 2017-2020 (ERSSTv5: -0.002 to +0.030). At 53 TAO/TRITON moorings, ERSSTv6 minus buoy rose by +0.116 C (95% interval 0.077-0.154; ERSSTv5 +0.004). Argo does not show the step clearly because of its own 2016 step. The step makes 2019 the ERSSTv6 record year (2019 minus 2016 = +0.046 C); after homogenisation 2016 is warmer by 0.018 C, as in the other products. It raises the ERSSTv6 2001-2022 trend from 0.143 to 0.178 C per decade, the acceleration coefficient from 0.023 to 0.0385 K per decade^2 (the largest of eight products), and the 2019-23 rate from 0.218 to 0.272 C per decade. NOAAGlobalTemp v6.1 minus v6.0 is +0.022 C higher in 2017-2020 than in 2013-2016. A relative Nino 3.4 index (RONI type) changes by only -0.011 C, but an absolute index is +0.067 C too warm in 2017-2020. With ERSSTv6 the 1982-2022 east-Pacific and west-east gradient trends stay outside all 112 CMIP6 members. Limitations: the cause is not found; ICOADS R3.0.2 platform counts show no jump at the step dates, and no documented ERSSTv6 change is in January 2017. Steps that ERSSTv5 and ERSSTv6 share cannot be assigned uniquely. Buoys are ERSST inputs.
